_readme: Copy to data/filters.json and edit. This file decides WHICH FEEDS EXIST: every key under 'feeds' is a feed's rkey, which must match the record key you publish it under. It is read at startup to build the routes, then hot-reloaded within ~10s of saving — editing an existing feed takes effect immediately, but adding or removing a feed needs a restart (the service logs a warning if you forget). A broken edit is rejected as a whole: the previous config is kept and the error is logged (docker logs feedgen). Each feed matches by includePatterns, by includeDids, or by both; a feed with neither is refused, since it would match the entire firehose. Patterns are JS RegExp with default flags 'iu' — inline flags like (?i) are Python/Go syntax and a SyntaxError here, so strip them (the 'i' is already applied). Each pattern's 'target' picks what it is tested against: 'text', 'text|alt_text', or 'text|alt_text|link' (link = the external card's url/title/description plus link facets); defaults are text|alt_text for include and text|alt_text|link for exclude. Toggles gifPosts/quotePosts/selfLabeledPosts accept allow | exclude | only. Replies are always dropped. Optional excludeListUri is the at:// URI of a Bluesky moderation list whose members' posts are dropped from that feed (refreshed hourly; several feeds naming the same list share one fetch). retention is {type:'hours'|'count', value:N}, default 72 hours. Optional pinnedPost is the at:// URI of a post to serve first on the feed's first page, carrying the 'Pinned' badge; it is suppressed from its ordinary position so it never appears twice, and it need not match the feed's filters.

my-feed._pinnedPost: Optional, omitted here so this example ships without a dead pin. Add "pinnedPost": "at://did:plc:.../app.bsky.feed.post/..." to show that post first, with the client's 'Pinned' badge.

includePatterns.comment: hashtag in the post body only — an image alt reading 'latte art' must not qualify

excludePatterns.comment: keep promos out, including ones that only appear in the link card

my-author-feed._comment: No patterns: this feed is every non-reply post by the listed accounts — useful for mirroring a bot or a single author. Keeps the newest 500 posts instead of a time window.
